sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Heard learned advocate Mr.S.M.Sojatwala with learned advocate Mr.Krutarth Desai appearing on behalf of the appellants, learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr.J.K.Shah appearing on behalf of the respondent-State and learned advocate Ms.Mahima Brahmbhatt appearing on behalf of respondent no.2.

1 2. Rule.

sentences.text: Learned APP waives service of rule on behalf of the respondent-State and learned advocate Ms.Brahmbhatt waives service of rule on behalf of respondent no.2.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/2575/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined 3.

The appellants have filed these appeals under Section 14(A) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 for enlarging the appellants on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No. 11199038250394/2025 registered with Nabipur Police Station, District Bharuch, for the offence punishable under Sections 115(2), 351(2), 333,
324(6), 189(2), 189(4), 190, 191(2), 75(1)(i) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Sections 3(1)(r),
3(1)(s), 3(2)(va), 3(1)(g), 3(1)(w)(i) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 and Section 135 of the Gujarat Police Act.
4. Learned advocate for the appellants would submit that considering the role attributed to the appellants, and nature of the allegation levelled, the appellants may be enlarged on regular bail.
It is further submitted that since the charge- sheet is filed, no useful purpose would be served by keeping the appellants in jail for indefinite period.

It is further contended that the appellants are ready and willing to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court if NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/2575/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined released on bail.

5. As against the same, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent - State and learned advocate Ms.Brahmbhatt for respondent no.2 have vehemently objected to the grant of regular bail.

Learned APP has submitted that looking to the nature of offence and the role attributed to the present appellants as coming out from the charge-sheet, this Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the appellants and the appeal may be dismissed.
6. I have heard learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers.

Following aspects are considered:-
i.

The allegation being very serious inasmuch as the accused are alleged to have demolished part of the house of the complainant using JCB inter alia under the guise that the complainant had received the favourable order from the Court.
ii. It also appears that during the course of demolition, the complainant i.e. lady of the house had also got injuries.

iii. The fact that while there is no order of Court whereby NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/2575/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined the present complainant had been asked to vacate the premises and yet,
the appellants, in a highhanded manner, having demolished part of the residential accommodation, yet, this Court has also taken into consideration the fact that the accused are in police custody since July, 2025, charge-sheet having been filed and except appellant of Cr.M.A. 2576/2025 and appellant no.4 of Cr.M.A. 2580/2025,
none of the other appellants having any antecedents.
Salim Ahmedshah Diwan vs State Of Gujarat on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160918913/
2 iv.

entities.text: Salim Ahmedshah Diwan vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant of Cr.M.A. 2576/2025 having four antecedents wherein it is stated that in all antecedents, the appellant has been released on bail and whereas, it also appears that the antecedents are of the year 2018 to 2022.
v. The appellant no.4 of Cr.M.A. 2580/2025 having one antecedent of the year 2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 420 IPC etc. vi.

The fact that learned advocates for the appellants jointly submitting under instruction that the appellants would undertake that they would rebuilt the demolished portion of the house in question by bringing the same to its original condition within a period of two months from the date of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/2575/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined their release.
vii.
It is submitted in this regard that a contractor has already been engaged who has quoted Rs.6,00,000/- for the said reconstruction.

This Court has taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40.
7.

entities.text: Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the appellants in the First Information Report, without discussing the evidence in detail,
prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the appellants on regular bail.
8. Hence, the present appeals are allowed.

sentences.text: If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the learned Trial Court concerned will be free to take appropriate action in the matter.
10. Bail bond to be executed before the lower court having jurisdiction to try the case.

It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions in accordance with law.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/2575/2025 ORDER DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined 11.

At the stage of trial, the trial court shall not be influenced by any observations of this Court which are of preliminary nature made at this stage, only for the purpose of considering the appeal of the appellant for being released on regular bail.
12. The appeals are allowed in the aforesaid terms.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service is permitted.
